solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Suitable site to develop for real estate

parts.note: proper means suitable or fitting

indicators.note: letters that develop grow into a new shape, so the word site is rearranged

explanation.surface: An estate agent spots a suitable plot to build on for a property portfolio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develop' reads as building on the site, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Real estate is land and buildings, the plural holdings an owner has.

clue.text: Pipe repaired, the two left

indicators.note: left here means departed, so those letters go out of the word repaired

parts.note: two together make a pair

explanation.surface: A plumber's pipe has been fixed, though two problems remain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' reads as 'remaining' but means 'gone': PAIR leaves REPAIRED.
explanation.definitionFit: A reed is a musical pipe, or the hollow plant stem such pipes were made from.

clue.text: Run through — run through article

indicators.note: the letter for run passes through the middle of the word for article

parts.note: a piece is an article or item
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A repeated phrase, like a stage direction for a swordsman lunging through a newspaper item.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeat tempts a double definition; the second 'run through' splits into R and an insertion indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce something is to stab or pass right into it, the sense of skewering with a blade.

clue.text: With wild cat entering, animals after turning tail didn't remain impassive

indicators.note: the rearranged cat goes into the reversed animals
turning tail means facing the other way, so the animals are read backwards

parts.note: deer are animals

indicators.note: wild means the letters of cat run loose into a new order

explanation.surface: Animals flee from a wild cat and clearly don't stay calm about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning tail' looks like the deer fleeing, but it means read the word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To show a response or emotional reaction is the opposite of staying impassive.

clue.text: Gentleman — I must stand for a lady

indicators.note: in a down entry standing up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters go backwards

parts.note: sir is the title of a gentleman

explanation.surface: A man insists he must stand to give his seat to a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: SIR then I read upward gives the woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Iris is a female first name, so it stands for a particular woman.

clue.text: Caballero, at the inside, is a politician

indicators.note: at is put on the inside of the Spanish gentleman's title

parts.note: caballero is Spanish for a gentleman, addressed as señor

explanation.surface: A Spanish horseman with insider connections turns out to be a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: SEÑOR, the Spanish for Mr, holds AT.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a senate, an elected lawmaker.

clue.text: Regarding the stock, don't buy it

definitions.text: Regarding the stock, don't buy it

parts.words: Regarding the stock, don't buy it
parts.note: looking at goods displayed behind the glass of a shop front without purchasing anything

explanation.surface: Sounds like a broker's advice about shares: look but don't invest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' suggests the stock market, but means a shop's goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To browse the goods in a shop display without any intention of purchasing is exactly this pastime.

clue.text: Closing rounds

parts.note: the final call for drinks at a pub before closing time

explanation.walkthrough: 'rounds' suggests boxing, but means rounds of drinks bought at the pub before it shuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The barman's call for the final drinks of the night is the pub's closing round of service.

clue.text: Performer that's mad to retire

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: mad about something means avid, keen

explanation.surface: A performer who must be crazy to quit the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a celebrated singer, especially an opera prima donna, so a performer.

clue.text: I get a raven trained so it's not eating worms, for example

indicators.note: trained means the letters are put through a drill into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone teaches a pet raven to give up its diet of worms.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains from meat, worms included, follows a meat-free diet.

clue.text: In the thick of having fifth of brandy in a blur

indicators.note: the picked letter goes in the word for blur

parts.note: a mist is a haze that blurs things

indicators.note: the fifth letter of brandy is picked

explanation.surface: Someone in a brandy haze, deep in the thick of things.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the middle or among things is what 'in the thick of' means.

clue.text: Advised cheese given as nourishment

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese
fed means given food

explanation.surface: A dietary tip: cheese is recommended as food.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone instructions or information beforehand is to advise them on a task.

clue.text: Not mah-jong — mah!

parts.note: the letters of ham read back to front; gammon is a kind of ham, so the word for ham written backwards gives this clue word

explanation.surface: A dismissive retort: not mah-jong, just an exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as an instruction, 'ham back', and you get MAH.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are traditional board games, so this game is a different one from mah-jong.

clue.text: Actually that's not rusty

definitions.meaning: in reality, as things really turn out rather than in theory
with skills kept fresh through regular exercise

explanation.surface: Actually, it isn't rusty.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both 'in reality' and 'kept sharp by regular rehearsal'.

clue.text: Transfer figure in wood frame

indicators.note: the numeral sits in the frame made by the word for wood

parts.note: deal is pine or fir timber
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A picture set in a wooden frame being moved elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frame' says DEAL surrounds C.
explanation.definitionFit: A decal is a design printed so that it can be transferred onto another surface.

clue.text: Fight for jobs, when many left the services?

definitions.meaning: jobs are posts, and a fight is a war, so a struggle over posts
the period after a conflict, when soldiers were demobilised

explanation.surface: Demobbed troops fighting for scarce jobs after the conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: The years following a war, when forces were demobbed, are this period.

clue.text: Shoes — large number in the clutches of little guys that chew them?

indicators.note: the numeral is held in the grip of the young dogs

parts.note: pups, young dogs, chew shoes
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Lots of shoes in the jaws of puppies that gnaw them.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumps are light slip-on shoes, such as plimsolls or court shoes.

clue.text: Object that's a little less than decorous

indicators.note: a little less means a letter short, so the end comes off the synonym

parts.note: demure means modest and decorous

explanation.surface: Something only slightly short of seemly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To demur is to raise an objection or show reluctance.

clue.text: Manage to catch by one's tail

parts.note: to cop is to catch or nab

indicators.note: the tail of the word one is its final letter, picked here

explanation.surface: Managing to grab something by its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to deal with something successfully, to get by.

clue.text: Second person spelling 'article' with two Es

parts.note: the is the definite article
adding one more E gives the article two of them

explanation.surface: A spelling lesson about writing an article with an extra E.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second person' is grammatical, not a runner-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Thee is the old object form of 'thou', the second-person singular pronoun.

clue.text: For 'Safety Devices', contains additional material

parts.note: has means contains
PS, postscript, is material added to a letter

explanation.surface: A safety manual whose appendix contains extra material.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasps are hinged metal fastenings secured by a padlock, devices for keeping doors safe.

clue.text: With look that's in, spent dosh for personal grooming

indicators.note: the look goes in the jumbled cash
spent money is scattered, so these letters change order

parts.note: an air is a look or manner

explanation.surface: Someone splashed cash to get the fashionable look.
explanation.walkthrough: DOSH is British slang for money; 'spent' scatters it, with the look slotted after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairstyles are a matter of personal grooming, ways of arranging one's locks.

clue.text: Spotted as it wanders back home

indicators.note: letters that wander roam into a new order
back means the word for home is read backwards

parts.note: a den is a home or lair

explanation.surface: Something seen as it strays back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanders' gives STAI from AS IT; DEN reversed gives NED.
explanation.definitionFit: Stained means marked with spots or blemishes.

clue.text: A Gallic translation would be 'très froid'

indicators.note: a translation turns the words into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: French: a translation of 'very cold' from the Gallic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'très froid' is French for 'very cold'.
explanation.definitionFit: Icy, extremely chilly: the French phrase means very cold.

clue.text: Flight announced from Eurasian ecoregion

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word is used for its sound

parts.note: a flight of stairs is a set of steps

explanation.surface: A flight departure being called for somewhere in Eurasia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' looks like air travel but means stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The vast grassland plains stretching across Eastern Europe and Central Asia are this ecoregion.

clue.text: English playwright depicting Greek character and notorious Roman one

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
Nero was the infamous Roman emperor

explanation.surface: A dramatist portraying a Greek and an infamous Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Wing Pinero wrote Victorian farces such as The Magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Arthur Wing Pinero was an English dramatist of the late 19th century.

clue.text: Less lustrous. That's what's wrong

definitions.meaning: more dull, comparing a matt finish
the trouble, as in 'what's up with you?'

explanation.surface: Something's lost its shine, and that's the problem.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of matt means duller, and the noun means the trouble or problem.

clue.text: A second and first-class returns from the continent

indicators.note: returns means comes back, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: A1 means first-class, here written AI

explanation.surface: A second-class and a first-class ticket bought for the trip back from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is first-rate; the numeral 1 doubles as letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest of the world's continents.

clue.text: Seven seen off, how many will be left?

definitions.text: Seven seen off, how many will be left?

parts.words: Seven seen off, how many will be left?
parts.note: remove the letters of seen from seven and V remains, the Roman numeral for this number

explanation.surface: A subtraction puzzle: seven gone, how many stay?
explanation.walkthrough: Arithmetic says none; strike S,E,E,N from SEVEN and V is left, the Roman numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman numeral V, the letter left over, stands for this number.

clue.text: I dither ineptly, about to do the wrong thing, get cut off

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about, around, the wrongdoing
done ineptly, the letters are clumsily rearranged

parts.note: to sin is to do wrong

explanation.surface: A dithering heir fears being cut off for misbehaving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ineptly' rearranges I DITHER into DIHERIT, which goes about SIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To disinherit is to cut an heir off, removing the right to inherit.

clue.text: Our forfeiting right to child — that hurt!

indicators.note: forfeiting means giving up, so the letter is lost

explanation.surface: A parent who loses rights over a child cries out in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of sudden pain, said when something hurt.

clue.text: Watches closely as long-term partnership has foundered

parts.note: in cricket a stand is a long partnership between two batsmen
's is short for has
over means finished, as a failed venture

explanation.surface: A long marriage has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a stand is a long batting partnership; once it is broken, the stand is over.
explanation.definitionFit: To supervise someone by hovering beside them is to stand over them.
